अंतिम उत्तर: केवल I, II और IV सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT4_Q08 - Autonomic cardiovascular regulation and pathophysiological disorders

questiontext.text:
Given below are four statements:

Statement I: Sympathetic neural signals released by the cardiac centre in the medulla oblongata increase the heart rate and the strength of ventricular contraction.

Statement II: Parasympathetic neural signals accelerate the speed of conduction of action potentials and increase the overall cardiac output.

Statement III: Coronary artery disease (atherosclerosis) results from luminal narrowing caused by deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol, and fibrous tissue.

Statement IV: Heart failure is a state where the heart fails to pump blood effectively to meet metabolic demands and is distinct from cardiac arrest.

Select the correct option from the following:

नीचे चार कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: मेडुला ऑबलागेटा में स्थित हृदय केंद्र द्वारा जारी अनुकंपी तंत्रिका संकेत हृदय दर और निलय संकुचन की शक्ति को बढ़ाते हैं।

कथन II: परानुकंपी तंत्रिका संकेत क्रिया विभव के संवहन की गति को तेज करते हैं और समग्र हृदय निकास को बढ़ाते हैं।

कथन III: कोरोनरी धमनी रोग (एथेरोस्क्लेरोसिस) कैल्शियम, वसा, कोलेस्ट्रॉल और रेशेदार ऊतकों के जमाव के कारण धमनियों की गुहा संकरी होने से होता है।

कथन IV: हृदय पात (हार्ट फेलियर) वह अवस्था है जिसमें हृदय शरीर की आवश्यकताओं के अनुसार पर्याप्त रक्त पंप करने में विफल रहता है और यह कार्डियक अरेस्ट से भिन्न होता है।

निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
Cardioacceleratory sympathetic fibers innervating nodal and myocardial tissues release catecholamines, boosting chronotropy (rate) and inotropy (contractile strength). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
Parasympathetic stimulation through vagal pathways slows nodal pacing, retards atrioventricular conduction velocity, and decreases cardiac output. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
Coronary artery disease (atherosclerosis) stems from progressive atheromatous plaque deposition containing lipids, cholesterol crystals, calcium, and collagen within coronary arterial walls. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement IV
Heart failure is defined by myocardial pump insufficiency (often resulting in congestion), whereas cardiac arrest represents total cessation of electrical and mechanical cardiac beating. Therefore, Statement IV is correct.

Final Answer: I, III and IV only are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
मेडुला के केंद्र से आने वाले अनुकंपी तंत्रिका संकेत हृदय स्पंदन दर और निलय संकुचन बल को बढ़ाकर हृदय निकास को बढ़ाते हैं। अतः, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
परानुकंपी तंत्रिका संकेत क्रिया विभव के संवहन की गति और हृदय स्पंदन दर को कम करते हैं, न कि बढ़ाते हैं। अतः, कथन II गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
कोरोनरी धमनी रोग में धमनियों की गुहा में वसा, कोलेस्ट्रॉल, रेशेदार ऊतक और कैल्शियम के जमाव से रक्त प्रवाह बाधित होता है। अतः, कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: कथन IV का मूल्यांकन
हृदय पात में हृदय अपर्याप्त रक्त पंप करता है, जबकि कार्डियक अरेस्ट में हृदय का धड़कना पूरी तरह से रुक जाता है। अतः, कथन IV सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल I, III और IV सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENTMULTI_Q01 - Fluid matrix and formed element characteristics of blood

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding body fluids and circulation:

Statement I: Blood is a specialised connective tissue consisting of a fluid matrix, plasma, and formed elements.

Statement II: Plasma constitutes nearly 55 per cent of whole blood, while formed elements make up nearly 45 per cent.

Statement III: Fibrinogens are major plasma proteins essential for the clotting or coagulation of blood.

Statement IV: A healthy adult man has on average 5 millions to 5.5 millions of erythrocytes (RBCs) mm⁻³ of blood.

Statement V: Mature mammalian erythrocytes possess a large spherical nucleus and numerous mitochondria.

Select the correct option from the following:

शारीरिक तरल और परिसंचरण के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: रक्त एक विशेष संयोजी ऊतक है जिसमें एक तरल मैट्रिक्स, प्लाज्मा और संघटित तत्व (फॉर्म्ड एलीमेंट्स) होते हैं।

कथन II: प्लाज्मा संपूर्ण रक्त का लगभग 55 प्रतिशत भाग बनाता है, जबकि संघटित तत्व लगभग 45 प्रतिशत भाग बनाते हैं।

कथन III: फाइब्रिनोजेन प्रमुख प्लाज्मा प्रोटीन हैं जो रक्त के थक्का जमने या स्कंदन के लिए आवश्यक होते हैं।

कथन IV: एक स्वस्थ वयस्क पुरुष में औसतन 5 से 5.5 मिलियन लाल रक्त कणिकाएं (RBC) प्रति घन मिलीमीटर रक्त में होती हैं।

कथन V: परिपक्व स्तनधारी एरिथ्रोसाइट्स में एक बड़ा गोलाकार केंद्रक और कई माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया पाए जाते हैं।

निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
Blood is classified histologically as a fluid connective tissue comprising extracellular liquid matrix (plasma) and suspension of cellular components (formed elements). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
In healthy humans, plasma accounts for approximately 55 percent of total blood volume, and formed elements comprise the remaining 45 percent. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
Fibrinogens represent soluble circulating procoagulant proteins that are converted into insoluble fibrin strands during coagulation. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement IV
Normal erythrocyte concentration in healthy adult males typically spans 5.0 to 5.5 million per cubic millimeter of blood. Therefore, Statement IV is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Statement V
During mammalian erythropoiesis, maturing erythrocytes expel the nucleus and other organelles to maximize intracellular space for hemoglobin. Therefore, Statement V is incorrect.

Final Answer: I, II, III and IV only are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
रक्त एक विशेष प्रकार का तरल संयोजी ऊतक है जिसमें प्लाज्मा और संघटित तत्व शामिल होते हैं। अतः, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
मानव रक्त में प्लाज्मा लगभग 55 प्रतिशत तथा संघटित तत्व (RBC, WBC, प्लेटलेट्स) लगभग 45 प्रतिशत होते हैं। अतः, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
फाइब्रिनोजेन महत्वपूर्ण प्लाज्मा प्रोटीन हैं जो रक्त स्कंदन के लिए आवश्यक होते हैं। अतः, कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: कथन IV का मूल्यांकन
स्वस्थ वयस्क पुरुष में RBC की सामान्य संख्या 5 से 5.5 मिलियन प्रति घन मिमी रक्त होती है। अतः, कथन IV सही है।

चरण 5: कथन V का मूल्यांकन
स्तनधारियों की परिपक्व RBC में केंद्रक तथा माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया अनुपस्थित होते हैं ताकि हीमोग्लोबिन के लिए अधिकतम स्थान मिल सके। अतः, कथन V गलत है।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल I, II, III और IV सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENTMULTI_Q02 - Leucocyte subpopulation functions and thrombocyte formation

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding body fluids and circulation:

Statement I: Neutrophils are the most abundant leucocytes, constituting 60-65 per cent of the total WBC count.

Statement II: Basophils constitute 0.5-1 per cent of WBCs and secrete histamine, serotonin, and heparin during inflammatory reactions.

Statement III: Monocytes are non-phagocytic agranulocytes that synthesize circulating antibodies.

Statement IV: Eosinophils (2-3 per cent) resist infections and are intimately associated with allergic reactions.

Statement V: Platelets (thrombocytes) are cell fragments produced from megakaryocytes in the bone marrow.

Select the correct option from the following:

शारीरिक तरल और परिसंचरण के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: न्यूट्रोफिल सबसे प्रचुर मात्रा में पाए जाने वाले श्वेताणु हैं, जो कुल WBC का 60-65 प्रतिशत भाग बनाते हैं।

कथन II: बेसोफिल WBC का 0.5-1 प्रतिशत भाग बनाते हैं और शोथकारी प्रतिक्रियाओं के दौरान हिस्टामाइन, सेरोटोनिन और हेपरिन का स्राव करते हैं।

कथन III: मोनोसाइट्स अभक्षकाणु (नॉन-फैगोसाइटिक) अकणिकाणु होते हैं जो परिसंचारी एंटीबॉडी का संश्लेषण करते हैं।

कथन IV: इओसिनोफिल (2-3 प्रतिशत) संक्रमण का विरोध करते हैं और एलर्जी प्रतिक्रियाओं से गहराई से जुड़े होते हैं।

कथन V: प्लेटलेट्स (थ्रोम्बोसाइट्स) अस्थि मज्जा में मेगाकैरियोसाइट्स से उत्पन्न होने वाले कोशिका खंड हैं।

निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
Neutrophils represent 60 to 65 percent of circulating leucocytes, acting as primary granulocytic phagocytes. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
Basophils are the least abundant leucocytes (0.5 to 1 percent) and secrete bioactive inflammatory mediators including histamine, heparin, and serotonin. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
Monocytes (6 to 8 percent) are dedicated phagocytic cells that ingest foreign microbes; antibodies are synthesized by B lymphocytes and plasma cells. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement IV
Eosinophils account for 2 to 3 percent of WBCs and participate in antiparasitic immunity and allergic hypersensitivity. Therefore, Statement IV is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Statement V
Thrombocytes are cytoplasmic fragments derived from polyploid bone marrow giant cells called megakaryocytes. Therefore, Statement V is correct.

Final Answer: I, II, IV and V only are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
न्यूट्रोफिल कुल श्वेताणुओं का 60-65 प्रतिशत बनाते हैं और प्राथमिक भक्षण कोशिकाएं होते हैं। अतः, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
बेसोफिल सबसे कम (0.5-1 प्रतिशत) होते हैं और हिस्टामाइन, सेरोटोनिन व हेपरिन स्रावित कर शोथकारी प्रतिक्रियाओं में भाग लेते हैं। अतः, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
मोनोसाइट्स भक्षकाणु (फैगोसाइटिक) होते हैं जो रोगाणुओं को नष्ट करते हैं; एंटीबॉडी का निर्माण B-लिम्फोसाइट्स द्वारा होता है। अतः, कथन III गलत है।

चरण 4: कथन IV का मूल्यांकन
इओसिनोफिल 2-3 प्रतिशत होते हैं, जो संक्रमण का प्रतिरोध करते हैं तथा एलर्जी प्रतिक्रियाओं से जुड़े हैं। अतः, कथन IV सही है।

चरण 5: कथन V का मूल्यांकन
प्लेटलेट्स अस्थि मज्जा की विशेष कोशिकाओं, मेगाकैरियोसाइट्स, के विखंडन से बनती हैं। अतः, कथन V सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल I, II, IV और V सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENTMULTI_Q03 - Morphological septa chambers and valvular organization of heart

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding body fluids and circulation:

Statement I: The human heart is protected by a double-walled membranous bag called pericardium enclosing pericardial fluid.

Statement II: A thin, muscular inter-atrial septum separates the right and left atria.

Statement III: The bicuspid or mitral valve guards the atrioventricular aperture between the right atrium and the right ventricle.

Statement IV: Semilunar valves guard the openings of the right and left ventricles into the pulmonary artery and the aorta respectively.

Statement V: Cardiac valves ensure strictly unidirectional flow of blood and prevent backward regurgitation.

Select the correct option from the following:

शारीरिक तरल और परिसंचरण के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: मानव हृदय एक दोहरी भित्ति वाली झिल्लीदार थैली से सुरक्षित रहता है जिसे पेरीकार्डियम कहते हैं, जिसमें पेरीकार्डियल तरल भरा होता है।

कथन II: एक पतली, पेशीय अंतर-आलिंद पट (इंटर-एट्रियल सेप्टम) दाएं और बाएं आलिंद को अलग करती है।

कथन III: द्विकपर्दी (मिट्रल) कपाट दाएं आलिंद और दाएं निलय के बीच के आलिंद-निलय छिद्र की रक्षा करता है।

कथन IV: अर्धचंद्र कपाट क्रमशः फुफ्फुसीय धमनी और महाधमनी में दाएं और बाएं निलय के निकास द्वारों की रक्षा करते हैं।

कथन V: हृदय के कपाट रक्त के एकदिशीय प्रवाह को सुनिश्चित करते हैं और विपरीत प्रवाह (उल्टे बहाव) को रोकते हैं।

निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
The heart is enveloped by the double-layered pericardial sac, which contains serous pericardial fluid to lubricate cardiac movements. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
The internal partition between the right and left atrial chambers is formed by the thin muscular inter-atrial septum. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
The tricuspid valve guards the right atrioventricular opening, while the bicuspid (mitral) valve guards the left atrioventricular opening. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement IV
Semilunar valves are located at the base of both great outflow vessels (the pulmonary trunk and aorta) to prevent ventricular backflow. Therefore, Statement IV is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Statement V
Cardiac valves open in response to downstream pressure gradients and close against upstream reversals, guaranteeing unidirectional flow from atria to ventricles and ventricles to arteries. Therefore, Statement V is correct.

Final Answer: I, II, IV and V only are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
हृदय दोहरी झिल्ली वाली पेरीकार्डियम थैली द्वारा सुरक्षित होता है, जिसमें पेरीकार्डियल तरल भरा होता है। अतः, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
दाएं और बाएं आलिंद के बीच एक पतली पेशीय अंतर-आलिंद पट पाई जाती है। अतः, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
दाएं आलिंद और दाएं निलय के बीच त्रिकपर्दी कपाट होता है, जबकि द्विकपर्दी कपाट बाएं आलिंद और बाएं निलय के बीच होता है। अतः, कथन III गलत है।

चरण 4: कथन IV का मूल्यांकन
फुफ्फुसीय धमनी और महाधमनी के आधार पर अर्धचंद्र कपाट उपस्थित होते हैं। अतः, कथन IV सही है।

चरण 5: कथन V का मूल्यांकन
हृदय कपाट रक्त को केवल एक दिशा में बहने देते हैं और उल्टे बहाव को रोकते हैं। अतः, कथन V सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल I, II, IV और V सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENTMULTI_Q04 - Comparative patterns of circulation across animal phyla

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding body fluids and circulation:

Statement I: An open circulatory system is present in arthropods and molluscs, where blood empties into large sinuses.

Statement II: Annelids and chordates have a closed circulatory system in which blood is continuously circulated through closed blood vessels.

Statement III: Fishes possess a 2-chambered heart that pumps deoxygenated blood to gills, exhibiting single circulation.

Statement IV: Birds and mammals possess a 4-chambered heart and show incomplete double circulation due to partial ventricular mixing.

Statement V: In amphibians and reptiles (except crocodiles), oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix in a single ventricle.

Select the correct option from the following:

शारीरिक तरल और परिसंचरण के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: आर्थ्रोपोडा और मोलस्का में खुला परिसंचरण तंत्र होता है, जहां रक्त बड़े साइनस (कोटरों) में प्रवाहित होता है।

कथन II: एनेलिड्स और कॉर्डेट्स में बंद परिसंचरण तंत्र होता है जिसमें रक्त हमेशा रक्त वाहिकाओं के बंद जाल में घूमता है।

कथन III: मछलियों में 2-कक्षीय हृदय होता है जो विऑक्सीजनित रक्त को क्लोम में पंप करता है, जो एकल परिसंचरण प्रदर्शित करता है।

कथन IV: पक्षियों और स्तनधारियों में 4-कक्षीय हृदय होता है और वे निलय में आंशिक रक्त मिश्रण के कारण अपूर्ण दोहरा परिसंचरण प्रदर्शित करते हैं।

कथन V: उभयचरों और सरीसृपों (मगरमच्छ को छोड़कर) में ऑक्सीजनित और विऑक्सीजनित रक्त एक ही निलय में मिश्रित हो जाते हैं।

निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
In arthropods and non-cephalopod molluscs, the heart pumps hemolymph through open arterial sinuses directly bathing tissues. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
Annelids and chordates regulate fluid transport within an enclosed network of arteries, capillaries, and veins. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
Fishes possess a single atrium and a single ventricle; venous blood is pumped to gills for oxygenation and onward systemic distribution before returning to the heart. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement IV
Birds and mammals have completely partitioned ventricles and atria, completely separating pulmonary and systemic circuits without any mixing (complete double circulation). Therefore, Statement IV is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of Statement V
In amphibians and reptiles (except crocodiles), both atria drain into an undivided or incompletely divided ventricle where oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix. Therefore, Statement V is correct.

Final Answer: I, II, III and V only are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
आर्थ्रोपोडा और मोलस्का में रक्त बड़े कोटरों (साइनस) में पंप किया जाता है, जो खुला परिसंचरण कहलाता है। अतः, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
एनेलिड और कॉर्डेट जीवों में रक्त वाहिकाओं के बंद तंत्र में प्रवाहित होता है, जो बंद परिसंचरण कहलाता है। अतः, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
मछलियों में दो कक्षीय हृदय विऑक्सीजनित रक्त को क्लोम में भेजता है, जहां से यह शरीर में जाता है (एकल परिसंचरण)। अतः, कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: कथन IV का मूल्यांकन
पक्षियों और स्तनधारियों में पूर्ण दोहरा परिसंचरण होता है जिसमें रक्त का कोई मिश्रण नहीं होता है। अतः, कथन IV गलत है।

चरण 5: कथन V का मूल्यांकन
उभयचरों और सरीसृपों में एक ही निलय होने के कारण आलिंदों से आने वाला रक्त मिश्रित हो जाता है (अपूर्ण दोहरा परिसंचरण)। अतः, कथन V सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल I, II, III और V सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENTMULTI_Q05 - Cardiac cycle electromechanical phases and electrocardiography

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding body fluids and circulation:

Statement I: During joint diastole, all four chambers of the heart are relaxed and blood moves passively into ventricles through open AV valves.

Statement II: An action potential generated by the SAN stimulates atrial systole, increasing blood flow into the ventricles by about 30 per cent.

Statement III: The first heart sound ('lub') is generated by the rapid opening of the semilunar valves during early ventricular systole.

Statement IV: In a standard ECG, the QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles, which initiates ventricular contraction.

Statement V: By counting the number of QRS complexes in an ECG trace over a given time period, the heart rate can be determined.

Select the correct option from the following:

शारीरिक तरल और परिसंचरण के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: संयुक्त अनुशिथिलन (जॉइंट डायस्टोल) के दौरान, हृदय के चारों कक्ष शिथिल होते हैं और रक्त खुले AV कपाटों के माध्यम से निष्क्रिय रूप से निलयों में भरता है।

कथन II: SAN द्वारा उत्पन्न क्रिया विभव आलिंद प्रकुंचन को प्रेरित करता है, जिससे निलयों में रक्त का प्रवाह लगभग 30 प्रतिशत बढ़ जाता है।

कथन III: प्रथम हृदय ध्वनि ('लब') प्रारंभिक निलय प्रकुंचन के दौरान अर्धचंद्र कपाटों के तेजी से खुलने के कारण उत्पन्न होती है।

कथन IV: एक मानक ECG में, QRS संकुल निलयों के विध्रुवण को दर्शाता है, जो निलय संकुचन की शुरुआत करता है।

कथन V: एक निश्चित समय अवधि में ECG ट्रेस में QRS संकुलों की संख्या गिनकर हृदय स्पंदन दर का निर्धारण किया जा सकता है।

निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
During joint diastole, both atria and ventricles are relaxed, semilunar valves are closed, and atrioventricular valves are open, allowing passive ventricular filling. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
Depolarization initiated by the sino-atrial node triggers coordinated atrial contraction, delivering the final 30 percent of end-diastolic blood volume into the ventricles. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
The first heart sound ('lub') results from vibrations caused by the sudden closure of the atrioventricular (tricuspid and bicuspid) valves, not the opening of semilunar valves. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement IV
The QRS deflection wave on a surface electrocardiogram corresponds to progressive depolarization of the ventricular syncytium. Therefore, Statement IV is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Statement V
Because each ventricular contraction produces one distinct QRS complex, tallying QRS spikes per unit time yields the instantaneous heart rate. Therefore, Statement V is correct.

Final Answer: I, II, IV and V only are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
संयुक्त अनुशिथिलन में चारों कक्ष विश्राम अवस्था में होते हैं और रक्त शिराओं से आलिंदों के जरिए निलयों में स्वतंत्र रूप से भरता है। अतः, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
SAN के क्रिया विभव से आलिंद संकुचित होते हैं, जिससे निलय में रक्त का प्रवाह लगभग 30 प्रतिशत बढ़ जाता है। अतः, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
प्रथम हृदय ध्वनि ('लब') त्रिकपर्दी और द्विकपर्दी कपाटों के बंद होने से संबंधित है, कपाटों के खुलने से नहीं। अतः, कथन III गलत है।

चरण 4: कथन IV का मूल्यांकन
QRS संकुल निलयों के विध्रुवण का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है जो निलय संकुचन को प्रारंभ करता है। अतः, कथन IV सही है।

चरण 5: कथन V का मूल्यांकन
प्रत्येक निलय संकुचन एक QRS संकुल बनाता है, अतः दिए गए समय में QRS की संख्या से हृदय दर ज्ञात की जाती है। अतः, कथन V सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल I, II, IV और V सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENTMULTI_Q06 - Vascular histology portal routing and cardiovascular disorders

questiontext.text:
Given below are five statements regarding body fluids and circulation:

Statement I: Human arteries and veins are structurally composed of three layers: tunica intima, tunica media, and tunica externa.

Statement II: The tunica media, containing smooth muscle and elastic fibres, is comparatively thinner in veins than in arteries.

Statement III: The hepatic portal vein carries deoxygenated blood directly from the digestive tract into the systemic aorta.

Statement IV: Coronary artery disease (atherosclerosis) narrows the arterial lumen due to deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol, and fibrous tissue.

Statement V: Heart failure is a condition where the heart fails to pump blood effectively, often causing lung congestion, and is distinct from cardiac arrest.

Select the correct option from the following:

शारीरिक तरल और परिसंचरण के संबंध में नीचे पाँच कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: मानव धमनियां और शिराएं संरचनात्मक रूप से तीन परतों से बनी होती हैं: ट्यूनिका इंटिमा, ट्यूनिका मीडिया और ट्यूनिका एक्सटर्ना।

कथन II: चिकनी पेशियों और प्रत्यास्थ तंतुओं से युक्त ट्यूनिका मीडिया परत धमनियों की तुलना में शिराओं में अपेक्षाकृत पतली होती है।

कथन III: हेपेटिक पोर्टल शिरा पाचन तंत्र से विऑक्सीजनित रक्त को सीधे महाधमनी (एओर्टा) में ले जाती है।

कथन IV: कोरोनरी धमनी रोग (एथेरोस्क्लेरोसिस) कैल्शियम, वसा, कोलेस्ट्रॉल और रेशेदार ऊतक के जमाव के कारण धमनी गुहा को संकरा कर देता है।

कथन V: हृदय पात (हार्ट फेलियर) वह स्थिति है जहां हृदय प्रभावी रूप से रक्त पंप करने में विफल रहता है, जिससे अक्सर फेफड़ों में जमाव होता है, और यह कार्डियक अरेस्ट से भिन्न होता है।

निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Statement I
Microscopic examination of arteries and veins reveals three tunics: innermost endothelial intima, middle muscular media, and outer connective adventitia (externa). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement II
Because veins function under low hydrostatic pressures, the muscular and elastic tunica media is much thinner than in high-pressure muscular arteries. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement III
The hepatic portal vein routes blood from intestinal capillary beds to hepatic sinusoids in the liver, not directly into the systemic aorta. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement IV
Atherosclerosis represents coronary lumen stenosis resulting from fibrofatty atheromatous plaques composed of lipids, cholesterol, calcium, and collagen. Therefore, Statement IV is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Statement V
Congestive heart failure denotes insufficient myocardial output relative to metabolic demands (commonly leading to pulmonary congestion), distinct from sudden electrical cessation in cardiac arrest. Therefore, Statement V is correct.

Final Answer: I, II, IV and V only are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का मूल्यांकन
धमनियों और शिराओं में तीन परतें पाई जाती हैं: ट्यूनिका इंटिमा (भीतरी), ट्यूनिका मीडिया (मध्य) और ट्यूनिका एक्सटर्ना (बाहरी)। अतः, कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का मूल्यांकन
शिराओं में रक्त का दबाव कम होने के कारण ट्यूनिका मीडिया परत धमनियों की अपेक्षा पतली होती है। अतः, कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का मूल्यांकन
हेपेटिक पोर्टल शिरा आंत से रक्त को यकृत में ले जाती है, सीधे महाधमनी में नहीं। अतः, कथन III गलत है।

चरण 4: कथन IV का मूल्यांकन
एथेरोस्क्लेरोसिस में कैल्शियम, वसा, कोलेस्ट्रॉल और रेशेदार ऊतकों के जमाव से हृदय धमनियों की गुहा संकरी हो जाती है। अतः, कथन IV सही है।

चरण 5: कथन V का मूल्यांकन
हृदय पात में हृदय पर्याप्त रूप से रक्त पंप नहीं कर पाता जिससे फेफड़ों में जमाव हो जाता है; यह कार्डियक अरेस्ट से अलग है। अतः, कथन V सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल I, II, IV और V सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MATCH_LIST_Q01 - Physiological roles of major plasma proteins

questiontext.text:
Match the items in Column I with their corresponding descriptions in Column II regarding plasma proteins and plasma constituents:

Column I (Plasma Protein / Component) Column II (Primary Function or Definition)
(A) Fibrinogen(I) Maintenance of osmotic balance
(B) Globulins(II) Plasma lacking coagulation factors
(C) Albumins(III) Clotting or coagulation of blood
(D) Serum(IV) Defense mechanisms of the body

Select the correct match from the options given:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Role of Fibrinogen
Fibrinogen is a high-molecular-weight soluble plasma protein synthesized by the liver. Upon activation during hemostasis, it is converted into insoluble fibrin threads that form a meshwork trapping blood cells, thereby facilitating the clotting or coagulation of blood.

Step 2: Role of Globulins
Globulins are a diverse group of serum proteins comprising immunoglobulins (antibodies) and transport proteins that are primarily involved in defense mechanisms of the body against infectious agents.

Step 3: Role of Albumins
Albumins constitute approximately 60 percent of total plasma proteins and are the major determinants of plasma oncotic pressure, playing an indispensable role in the maintenance of osmotic balance between vascular and tissue spaces.

Step 4: Definition of Serum
Serum represents the liquid fraction of blood that remains after whole blood is allowed to clot; it is identical in solute composition to plasma but completely lacks fibrinogen and other coagulation factors.

Step 5: Synthesis of Correct Associations
Fibrinogen corresponds to clotting or coagulation of blood; Globulins correspond to defense mechanisms of the body; Albumins correspond to maintenance of osmotic balance; and Serum corresponds to plasma lacking coagulation factors.

Final Answer: Fibrinogen pairs with clotting or coagulation of blood; Globulins pair with defense mechanisms of the body; Albumins pair with maintenance of osmotic balance; Serum pairs with plasma lacking coagulation factors.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MATCH_LIST_Q02 - Functional characteristics of human leukocyte types

questiontext.text:
Match the items in Column I with their corresponding descriptions in Column II regarding human leukocytes and their specialized functions:

Column I (Leukocyte Type) Column II (Functional Role or Characteristic)
(A) Neutrophils(I) Secrete histamine and heparin in inflammatory reactions
(B) Basophils(II) Specialized cells responsible for immune responses
(C) Eosinophils(III) Most abundant phagocytic white blood cells
(D) Lymphocytes(IV) Resist infections and associated with allergic reactions

Select the correct match from the options given:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Functional Role of Neutrophils
Neutrophils are polymorphonuclear granulocytes constituting 60 to 65 percent of circulating leukocytes, functioning as the primary phagocytic responders that ingest invading pathogens.

Step 2: Functional Role of Basophils
Basophils represent 0.5 to 1 percent of white blood cells and synthesize and release inflammatory mediators, including histamine, serotonin, and the anticoagulant heparin.

Step 3: Functional Role of Eosinophils
Eosinophils comprise 2 to 3 percent of leukocytes, containing hydrolytic granules specialized to combat parasitic infestations and participate in hypersensitivity and allergic reactions.

Step 4: Functional Role of Lymphocytes
Lymphocytes constitute 20 to 25 percent of white blood cells and differentiate into B and T cells that orchestrate antigen-specific adaptive immune responses.

Step 5: Synthesis of Correct Associations
Neutrophils correspond to most abundant phagocytic white blood cells; Basophils correspond to secreting histamine and heparin in inflammatory reactions; Eosinophils correspond to resisting infections and allergic reactions; and Lymphocytes correspond to immune responses.

Final Answer: Neutrophils pair with most abundant phagocytic white blood cells; Basophils pair with secreting histamine and heparin in inflammatory reactions; Eosinophils pair with resisting infections and allergic reactions; Lymphocytes pair with specialized cells responsible for immune responses.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MATCH_LIST_Q03 - Antigen and antibody distribution in blood

questiontext.text:
Match the items in Column I with their corresponding descriptions in Column II regarding ABO blood groups and their immunological markers:

Column I (ABO Blood Group) Column II (Antigens on Erythrocytes and Antibodies in Plasma)
(A) Blood group A(I) Carries both surface antigens A and B on RBCs and no antibodies in plasma
(B) Blood group B(II) Lacks surface antigens on RBCs and carries both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in plasma
(C) Blood group AB(III) Carries antigen B on RBCs and anti-A antibodies in plasma
(D) Blood group O(IV) Carries antigen A on RBCs and anti-B antibodies in plasma

Select the correct match from the options given:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Immunological Features of Group A
Individuals classified under blood group A express surface agglutinogen A on their red blood cell membranes and possess naturally occurring anti-B isoantibodies in their plasma.

Step 2: Immunological Features of Group B
Individuals of blood group B exhibit surface agglutinogen B on their erythrocytes and produce circulating anti-A isoantibodies in their plasma.

Step 3: Immunological Features of Group AB
Erythrocytes of group AB individuals express both surface antigen A and antigen B, but their plasma is devoid of both anti-A and anti-B antibodies, making them universal plasma recipients.

Step 4: Immunological Features of Group O
Group O individuals do not express surface antigen A or antigen B on their erythrocytes, while their circulating plasma contains both anti-A and anti-B antibodies, rendering them universal erythrocyte donors.

Step 5: Synthesis of Correct Associations
Blood group A corresponds to antigen A on RBCs and anti-B antibodies in plasma; Blood group B corresponds to antigen B on RBCs and anti-A antibodies in plasma; Blood group AB corresponds to both antigens on RBCs and no antibodies in plasma; and Blood group O corresponds to no surface antigens on RBCs and both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in plasma.

Final Answer: Blood group A pairs with antigen A on RBCs and anti-B antibodies in plasma; Blood group B pairs with antigen B on RBCs and anti-A antibodies in plasma; Blood group AB pairs with both antigens A and B on RBCs and no antibodies in plasma; Blood group O pairs with lack of surface antigens on RBCs and presence of both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in plasma.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MATCH_LIST_Q04 - Biochemical components of blood coagulation cascade

questiontext.text:
Match the items in Column I with their corresponding descriptions in Column II regarding the biochemical factors involved in the blood coagulation cascade:

Column I (Clotting Factor or Component) Column II (Biochemical Role in Hemostasis)
(A) Thrombokinase(I) Inactive plasma protein converted into active thrombin
(B) Prothrombin(II) Soluble plasma precursor cleaved to yield insoluble fibrin mesh
(C) Fibrinogen(III) Essential mineral cofactor required at multiple clotting steps
(D) Calcium ions(IV) Enzymatic complex generated by cascade of linked reactions

Select the correct match from the options given:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Biochemical Action of Thrombokinase
Thrombokinase is a multi-molecular enzymatic complex assembled through an extrinsic and intrinsic cascade of plasma and platelet factors following tissue trauma, serving to cleave prothrombin.

Step 2: Biochemical Action of Prothrombin
Prothrombin is an inactive circulating plasma zymogen that undergoes proteolytic activation by thrombokinase to yield active thrombin.

Step 3: Biochemical Action of Fibrinogen
Fibrinogen is a large soluble plasma protein that is enzymatically cleaved by thrombin into fibrin monomers, which polymerize to create a stable insoluble fibrillar meshwork.

Step 4: Biochemical Action of Calcium Ions
Divalent calcium ions act as an essential cofactor facilitating prothrombinase assembly, tenase activation, and fibrin cross-linking throughout the hemostatic cascade.

Step 5: Synthesis of Correct Associations
Thrombokinase corresponds to the enzymatic complex generated by cascade; Prothrombin corresponds to the inactive protein converted into thrombin; Fibrinogen corresponds to the soluble precursor cleaved to form fibrin mesh; and Calcium ions correspond to the essential mineral cofactor.

Final Answer: Thrombokinase pairs with enzymatic complex generated by cascade of linked reactions; Prothrombin pairs with inactive plasma protein converted into active thrombin; Fibrinogen pairs with soluble plasma precursor cleaved to yield insoluble fibrin mesh; Calcium ions pair with essential mineral cofactor required at multiple clotting steps.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MATCH_LIST_Q05 - Vertebrate classes and heart chamber patterns

questiontext.text:
Match the items in Column I with their corresponding descriptions in Column II regarding vertebrate heart anatomy and circulatory patterns:

Column I (Vertebrate Group) Column II (Cardiac Architecture and Flow Pathway)
(A) Fishes(I) Four-chambered heart in a reptilian exception
(B) Amphibians(II) Four-chambered heart with complete double circulation
(C) Crocodiles(III) Two-chambered heart with single circulation
(D) Birds and mammals(IV) Three-chambered heart with incomplete double circulation

Select the correct match from the options given:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Circulatory System of Fishes
Fishes feature a two-chambered heart comprising a single atrium and a single ventricle; deoxygenated blood pumped by the ventricle undergoes gill oxygenation and flows directly to tissues before returning, representing single circulation.

Step 2: Circulatory System of Amphibians
Amphibians possess a three-chambered heart with two atria and one common ventricle, where oxygenated pulmonary blood and deoxygenated systemic blood enter separately but mix prior to ejection, producing incomplete double circulation.

Step 3: Circulatory System of Crocodiles
Crocodilians depart from typical reptilian cardiac anatomy by possessing a completely partitioned four-chambered heart containing two atria and two ventricles.

Step 4: Circulatory System of Birds and Mammals
Birds and mammals possess fully separated four-chambered hearts with two atria and two ventricles, completely isolating pulmonary and systemic vascular circuits in true double circulation.

Step 5: Synthesis of Correct Associations
Fishes correspond to a two-chambered heart with single circulation; Amphibians correspond to a three-chambered heart with incomplete double circulation; Crocodiles correspond to a four-chambered heart in a reptilian exception; and Birds and mammals correspond to a four-chambered heart with complete double circulation.

Final Answer: Fishes pair with two-chambered heart with single circulation; Amphibians pair with three-chambered heart with incomplete double circulation; Crocodiles pair with four-chambered heart in a reptilian exception; Birds and mammals pair with four-chambered heart with complete double circulation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MATCH_LIST_Q06 - Anatomical positions of human cardiac valves

questiontext.text:
Match the items in Column I with their corresponding descriptions in Column II regarding the internal anatomy and valve locations of the human heart:

Column I (Cardiac Valve) Column II (Anatomical Aperture Guarded by Valve)
(A) Tricuspid valve(I) Opening between left atrium and left ventricle
(B) Bicuspid valve(II) Opening between right ventricle and pulmonary artery
(C) Aortic semilunar valve(III) Opening between right atrium and right ventricle
(D) Pulmonary semilunar valve(IV) Opening between left ventricle and systemic aorta

Select the correct match from the options given:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Anatomy of the Tricuspid Valve
The right atrioventricular opening is guarded by a valve formed of three fibrous cusps, designated the tricuspid valve, ensuring forward flow into the right ventricle.

Step 2: Anatomy of the Bicuspid Valve
The left atrioventricular opening is protected by a two-cusped structure designated the bicuspid or mitral valve, preventing backward flow into the left atrium during ventricular contraction.

Step 3: Anatomy of the Aortic Semilunar Valve
The exit of the left ventricle into the systemic aorta is guarded by pocket-like aortic semilunar cusps that close during ventricular diastole.

Step 4: Anatomy of the Pulmonary Semilunar Valve
The outlet of the right ventricle leading into the pulmonary trunk is guarded by pulmonary semilunar valves that prevent regurgitation of blood from pulmonary circulation.

Step 5: Synthesis of Correct Associations
Tricuspid valve corresponds to opening between right atrium and right ventricle; Bicuspid valve corresponds to opening between left atrium and left ventricle; Aortic semilunar valve corresponds to opening between left ventricle and systemic aorta; and Pulmonary semilunar valve corresponds to opening between right ventricle and pulmonary artery.

Final Answer: Tricuspid valve pairs with opening between right atrium and right ventricle; Bicuspid valve pairs with opening between left atrium and left ventricle; Aortic semilunar valve pairs with opening between left ventricle and systemic aorta; Pulmonary semilunar valve pairs with opening between right ventricle and pulmonary artery.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MATCH_LIST_Q07 - Electrical phases of a standard electrocardiogram

questiontext.text:
Match the items in Column I with their corresponding descriptions in Column II regarding waveforms of a standard electrocardiogram and their underlying cardiac events:

Column I (ECG Deflection) Column II (Underlying Electrophysiological Event)
(A) P-wave(I) Ventricular repolarisation returning musculature to resting state
(B) QRS complex(II) Marks the clinical conclusion of ventricular systole
(C) T-wave(III) Depolarisation of ventricles initiating ventricular systole
(D) End of T-wave(IV) Depolarisation of atria leading to atrial contraction

Select the correct match from the options given:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Electrophysiology of the P-wave
The P-wave is the first positive deflection on an electrocardiogram, representing the wave of electrical excitation or depolarization sweeping across both atria, which initiates atrial systole.

Step 2: Electrophysiology of the QRS Complex
The QRS complex represents rapid electrical depolarization across the ventricular myocardium, marking the onset of ventricular systole shortly after the Q wave.

Step 3: Electrophysiology of the T-wave
The T-wave is an upward deflection representing ventricular repolarization, during which ventricular myocytes recover from an excited state back to their resting membrane potential.

Step 4: Clinical Significance of the End of T-wave
The terminal baseline transition at the end of the T-wave marks the cessation of ventricular electrical repolarization and the conclusion of ventricular mechanical systole.

Step 5: Synthesis of Correct Associations
P-wave corresponds to depolarisation of atria; QRS complex corresponds to depolarisation of ventricles; T-wave corresponds to ventricular repolarisation; and End of T-wave corresponds to marks the clinical conclusion of ventricular systole.

Final Answer: P-wave pairs with depolarisation of atria leading to atrial contraction; QRS complex pairs with depolarisation of ventricles initiating ventricular systole; T-wave pairs with ventricular repolarisation returning musculature to resting state; End of T-wave pairs with marks the clinical conclusion of ventricular systole.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MATCH_LIST_Q08 - Components of the human cardiac conduction system

questiontext.text:
Match the items in Column I with their corresponding descriptions in Column II regarding the specialized nodal tissues of the cardiac conduction system:

Column I (Conducting System Element) Column II (Anatomical Location and Conducting Function)
(A) Sino-atrial node(I) Lower left corner of right atrium near atrioventricular septum
(B) Atrio-ventricular node(II) Crosses fibrous septum and divides atop interventricular septum into bundle branches
(C) Atrio-ventricular bundle(III) Minute terminal conducting arborizations distributed throughout ventricular myocardium
(D) Purkinje fibres(IV) Right upper corner of right atrium, generates 70-75 action potentials per minute

Select the correct match from the options given:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Role of the Sino-atrial Node
The sino-atrial node sits in the right upper wall of the right atrium; it possesses the highest intrinsic automaticity, discharging 70 to 75 action potentials per minute to serve as the cardiac pacemaker.

Step 2: Role of the Atrio-ventricular Node
The atrio-ventricular node is positioned in the lower left corner of the right atrium adjacent to the fibrous atrioventricular septum, relaying incoming atrial excitation toward the ventricles.

Step 3: Role of the Atrio-ventricular Bundle
The atrio-ventricular bundle (bundle of His) penetrates the fibrous atrioventricular ring, emerges on the crest of the interventricular septum, and bifurcates into right and left bundle branches.

Step 4: Role of the Purkinje Fibres
Purkinje fibres arise from the bundle branches and form a fine subendocardial arborization throughout both ventricular myocardial walls, propagating impulses rapidly for coordinated contraction.

Step 5: Synthesis of Correct Associations
Sino-atrial node corresponds to generating 70-75 action potentials in right upper atrium; Atrio-ventricular node corresponds to lower left right atrium; Atrio-ventricular bundle corresponds to crossing septum and dividing; and Purkinje fibres correspond to minute arborizations in ventricular walls.

Final Answer: Sino-atrial node pairs with right upper corner of right atrium, generates 70-75 action potentials per minute; Atrio-ventricular node pairs with lower left corner of right atrium near atrioventricular septum; Atrio-ventricular bundle pairs with crosses fibrous septum and divides atop interventricular septum into bundle branches; Purkinje fibres pair with minute terminal conducting arborizations distributed throughout ventricular myocardium.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MATCH_LIST_Q09 - Vascular circuits and histological vessel layers

questiontext.text:
Match the items in Column I with their corresponding descriptions in Column II regarding blood vessel histology, specialized portal systems, and circulatory circuits:

Column I (Circulatory Component) Column II (Histological or Anatomical Feature)
(A) Hepatic portal vein(I) Dedicated vascular network exclusively supplying and draining cardiac muscle
(B) Coronary circulation(II) Middle vascular coat with smooth muscle and elastic fibers, thinner in veins
(C) Tunica media(III) Carries nutrient-rich blood from digestive tract to liver before systemic return
(D) Tunica intima(IV) Innermost vascular coat consisting of simple squamous endothelium

Select the correct match from the options given:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Role of the Hepatic Portal Vein
The hepatic portal system forms a unique venous bypass wherein the hepatic portal vein collects deoxygenated, nutrient-rich blood from gastrointestinal viscera and routes it directly to liver sinusoids prior to caval delivery.

Step 2: Role of Coronary Circulation
Because heart muscle has immense metabolic demands, it is nourished by an exclusive coronary arterial and venous system that supplies and drains blood from the myocardium.

Step 3: Histology of Tunica Media
The tunica media constitutes the intermediate vascular layer made of circularly arranged smooth muscle cells and elastic fibers, being significantly thinner in veins than in systemic arteries.

Step 4: Histology of Tunica Intima
The tunica intima is the innermost tunic of the blood vessel wall, formed by a delicate single layer of squamous endothelium that provides a smooth, non-thrombogenic surface for blood flow.

Step 5: Synthesis of Correct Associations
Hepatic portal vein corresponds to carrying blood from digestive tract to liver; Coronary circulation corresponds to dedicated network supplying cardiac muscle; Tunica media corresponds to middle smooth muscle coat thinner in veins; and Tunica intima corresponds to innermost squamous endothelium.

Final Answer: Hepatic portal vein pairs with carries nutrient-rich blood from digestive tract to liver before systemic return; Coronary circulation pairs with dedicated vascular network exclusively supplying and draining cardiac muscle; Tunica media pairs with middle vascular coat with smooth muscle and elastic fibers, thinner in veins; Tunica intima pairs with innermost vascular coat consisting of simple squamous endothelium.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MATCH_LIST_Q10 - Clinical features of human cardiovascular disorders

questiontext.text:
Match the items in Column I with their corresponding descriptions in Column II regarding etiologies and manifestations of human circulatory disorders:

Column I (Circulatory Disorder) Column II (Diagnostic Hallmark and Clinical Manifestation)
(A) Hypertension(I) State wherein the heart does not pump blood effectively to meet bodily needs
(B) Atherosclerosis(II) Severe chest pain appearing when insufficient oxygen reaches heart muscle
(C) Angina pectoris(III) Repeated arterial blood pressure readings of 140/90 mm Hg or higher
(D) Heart failure(IV) Lumen of coronary arteries narrowed by deposits of calcium, fat, and fibrous tissue

Select the correct match from the options given:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Clinical Features of Hypertension
Hypertension is diagnosed when multiple resting sphygmomanometer readings show systolic pressures of 140 mm Hg or higher and diastolic pressures of 90 mm Hg or higher, straining vital organ perfusion.

Step 2: Clinical Features of Atherosclerosis
Atherosclerosis (coronary artery disease) involves the progressive accumulation of atheromatous plaques containing cholesterol, lipids, calcium, and fibrous connective tissue within coronary arteries, constricting their lumen.

Step 3: Clinical Features of Angina Pectoris
Angina pectoris presents with episodes of acute thoracic chest pain caused by transient myocardial ischemia when coronary flow fails to deliver sufficient oxygen to meet myocardial demand.

Step 4: Clinical Features of Heart Failure
Heart failure describes a functional deficit in which cardiac ventricles fail to generate sufficient forward stroke volume and cardiac output to satisfy metabolic demands of peripheral tissues, commonly causing pulmonary venous congestion.

Step 5: Synthesis of Correct Associations
Hypertension corresponds to blood pressure readings of 140/90 mm Hg or higher; Atherosclerosis corresponds to arterial lumen narrowed by lipid and calcium deposits; Angina pectoris corresponds to severe chest pain from insufficient oxygen delivery; and Heart failure corresponds to inability of heart to pump blood effectively to meet bodily needs.

Final Answer: Hypertension pairs with repeated arterial blood pressure readings of 140/90 mm Hg or higher; Atherosclerosis pairs with lumen of coronary arteries narrowed by deposits of calcium, fat, and fibrous tissue; Angina pectoris pairs with severe chest pain appearing when insufficient oxygen reaches heart muscle; Heart failure pairs with state wherein the heart does not pump blood effectively to meet bodily needs.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Chronological sequence of blood coagulation cascade events

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following biochemical and cellular events occurring during the mechanism of blood coagulation in the correct chronological sequence following tissue trauma or vascular injury:

(I) Conversion of inactive prothrombin into active thrombin by an enzyme complex in the presence of calcium ions.

(II) Formation of the enzyme complex thrombokinase through a cascade of linked enzymatic reactions.

(III) Stimulation of platelets and damaged tissues to release factors that initiate the coagulation mechanism.

(IV) Entanglement of dead and damaged formed elements within a network of threads to form a dark reddish-brown clot.

(V) Cleavage of soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads by thrombin.

Which of the following represents the correct sequential order of these events?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Initiation by Platelets and Damaged Tissue
Physical injury stimulates platelets and damaged vascular endothelium to release thromboplastic factors that trigger the clotting mechanism.

Step 2: Generation of the Thrombokinase Complex
These released factors activate a cascade process involving inactive plasma factors in a series of linked enzymic reactions, leading to the formation of the enzyme complex thrombokinase.

Step 3: Conversion of Prothrombin to Thrombin
In the presence of calcium ions, thrombokinase catalyses the conversion of the inactive plasma protein prothrombin into the active proteolytic enzyme thrombin.

Step 4: Formation of Insoluble Fibrin Threads
Thrombin acts enzymatically upon soluble fibrinogen in plasma, polymerising it into long insoluble threads of fibrin.

Step 5: Formation of the Coagulum
The insoluble fibrin threads create an intricate meshwork that traps erythrocytes, leukocytes, and damaged cellular debris, forming the definitive clot or coagulum that seals the wound.

Final Answer: The correct chronological sequence is release of initiation factors by platelets and injured tissue, followed by enzymatic formation of thrombokinase, conversion of prothrombin to active thrombin, conversion of fibrinogen into fibrin threads, and trapping of formed elements to form the clot.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Sequence of cardiac excitation and ventricular ejection

questiontext.text:
The following events take place during the transmission of cardiac excitation and the subsequent ventricular pumping phase of a human cardiac cycle:

(I) Transmission of the electrical impulse down the inter-ventricular septum along the bundle of His and spreading through the Purkinje fibres.

(II) Generation of an action potential by the sino-atrial node in the upper right wall of the right atrium.

(III) Sharp rise in ventricular pressure forcing open the semilunar valves to eject blood into the pulmonary artery and aorta.

(IV) Arrival and conduction of the action potential through the atrio-ventricular node.

(V) Onset of ventricular systole increasing intraventricular pressure and causing closure of the atrio-ventricular valves.

Which of the following represents the correct logical sequence of these events?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Initiation of Electrical Impulse at the Sino-Atrial Node
The sino-atrial node located in the right upper corner of the right atrium possesses the highest rate of autoexcitability (70 to 75 action potentials per minute). It initiates the cardiac cycle by generating an action potential that spreads across the atrial musculature, triggering atrial systole.

Step 2: Conduction to the Atrio-Ventricular Node
From the atria, the wave of depolarisation reaches the atrio-ventricular node situated in the lower left corner of the right atrium close to the atrio-ventricular septum, where it is briefly delayed before conducting toward the ventricles.

Step 3: Propagation Through the Bundle of His and Purkinje Fibres
The action potential enters the atrio-ventricular bundle (bundle of His) traversing the inter-ventricular septum, splitting into right and left bundle branches that distribute minute Purkinje fibres throughout the ventricular myocardium.

Step 4: Ventricular Contraction and Closure of Atrio-Ventricular Valves
The coordinated excitation of ventricular muscle fibres initiates ventricular systole. The immediate increase in intraventricular pressure forces blood toward the atria, which promptly closes the tricuspid and bicuspid (mitral) valves to prevent backflow, generating the first heart sound.

Step 5: Opening of Semilunar Valves and Ventricular Ejection
As ventricular myocardial contraction continues, intraventricular pressure surpasses the pressure within the major outflow tracts, forcing the semilunar valves of the pulmonary artery and systemic aorta open to eject blood into the circulation.

Final Answer: The correct chronological order is impulse initiation at the sino-atrial node, conduction through the atrio-ventricular node, transmission down the bundle of His and Purkinje fibres, closure of atrio-ventricular valves during early ventricular systole, and opening of semilunar valves for ventricular ejection.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q01 - Percentage contribution of plasma in human blood

questiontext.text: Blood is a specialized connective tissue consisting of a fluid matrix, plasma, and formed elements. What percentage of total blood volume is constituted by plasma?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Blood is a specialized fluid connective tissue composed of two major parts: the liquid matrix known as plasma and the cellular components collectively called formed elements.

Step 2: Evaluation of Blood Composition
In healthy human adults, plasma constitutes approximately 55 per cent of the total volume of blood, while formed elements (erythrocytes, leucocytes, and platelets) account for the remaining 45 per cent.

Final Answer: Plasma constitutes nearly 55 per cent of total human blood volume.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q02 - Major protein responsible for blood osmotic balance

questiontext.text: Which major plasma protein plays a primary physiological role in maintaining osmotic balance in human blood?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plasma proteins make up approximately 6 to 8 per cent of plasma. The major proteins include fibrinogens, globulins, and albumins, each serving distinct physiological roles.

Step 2: Evaluation of Protein Functions
Fibrinogens are essential for blood clotting; globulins participate in immune defense mechanisms; and albumins are primarily responsible for maintaining the colloid osmotic balance of blood.

Final Answer: Albumins are the major plasma proteins responsible for maintaining osmotic balance.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q03 - Average lifespan of human red blood cells

questiontext.text: What is the average lifespan of mature human erythrocytes in circulation before they are destroyed in the spleen?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Erythrocytes (red blood cells) are produced in the red bone marrow of adults and lose their nuclei during maturation to maximize room for haemoglobin.

Step 2: Evaluation of RBC Longevity
Lacking nuclei and metabolic repair organelles, human erythrocytes remain functionally active in peripheral circulation for an average lifespan of 120 days. Old and worn-out RBCs are subsequently filtered and destroyed in the spleen.

Final Answer: The average lifespan of human erythrocytes in circulation is 120 days.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q04 - Most abundant white blood cells in blood

questiontext.text: Among the different types of leucocytes present in normal human blood, which cells are the most abundant?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Leucocytes (white blood cells) are classified into granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils) and agranulocytes (lymphocytes, monocytes).

Step 2: Evaluation of Relative Abundance
Neutrophils are the most abundant white blood cells, representing 60 to 65 per cent of total leucocytes. In contrast, lymphocytes comprise 20 to 25 per cent, monocytes comprise 6 to 8 per cent, eosinophils comprise 2 to 3 per cent, and basophils comprise 0.5 to 1 per cent.

Final Answer: Neutrophils are the most abundant leucocytes, constituting 60 to 65 per cent of total white blood cells.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q05 - Bone marrow precursor cells of blood platelets

questiontext.text: Blood platelets (thrombocytes) are cell fragments produced from which specialized cells in the bone marrow?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Platelets, or thrombocytes, are circulating non-nucleated fragments essential for blood clotting and hemostasis.

Step 2: Evaluation of Origin
Platelets are formed in the red bone marrow by the fragmentation of mature giant precursor cells termed megakaryocytes.

Final Answer: Platelets are cell fragments produced from megakaryocytes in the bone marrow.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q06 - Universal recipient blood group in ABO system

questiontext.text: An individual whose red blood cells carry both antigen A and antigen B, but whose plasma lacks both anti-A and anti-B antibodies, belongs to which ABO blood group?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The ABO blood grouping system relies on the distribution of surface antigens on erythrocytes and natural antibodies in the plasma.

Step 2: Evaluation of Blood Group Characteristics
Group AB erythrocytes display both antigen A and antigen B, while their plasma contains neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies. Because their plasma does not clump incoming donor RBCs, group AB individuals can receive red blood cells from any ABO group and are termed universal recipients.

Final Answer: Individuals with both antigens A and B on red blood cells and no plasma antibodies belong to blood group AB.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q07 - Heart valve located between left chambers

questiontext.text: Which valve guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle in the human heart?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Atrioventricular valves ensure unidirectional forward flow of blood from the atria into the ventricles and prevent regurgitation during ventricular contraction.

Step 2: Evaluation of Anatomical Location
The opening between the right atrium and right ventricle is guarded by the tricuspid valve, whereas the opening between the left atrium and left ventricle is guarded by the bicuspid valve, also termed the mitral valve.

Final Answer: The bicuspid or mitral valve guards the opening between the left atrium and left ventricle.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q08 - Normal human resting cardiac cycle time duration

questiontext.text: In a healthy human individual with an average resting heart rate of 72 beats per minute, what is the duration of a single cardiac cycle?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A cardiac cycle comprises one complete sequence of contraction (systole) and relaxation (diastole) of cardiac chambers.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Calculation
With a resting heart rate of 72 beats per minute (60 seconds), the duration of one cardiac cycle is calculated as \(60\text{ s} / 72 \approx 0.833\text{ s}\), which is standardized in human physiology as 0.8 seconds.

Final Answer: The duration of a single cardiac cycle in a resting healthy human is 0.8 seconds.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q09 - Pumping and resting blood pressure threshold values

questiontext.text: In a standard resting blood pressure reading of \(120/80\text{ mm Hg}\), what do the values 120 and 80 represent respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Arterial blood pressure is recorded as two pressure limits corresponding to ventricular contraction and relaxation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pressure Limits
The value \(120\text{ mm Hg}\) denotes the systolic pressure, which is the peak pumping pressure during ventricular systole. The value \(80\text{ mm Hg}\) denotes the diastolic pressure, which is the minimum resting pressure maintained during ventricular diastole.

Final Answer: The values 120 and 80 represent systolic (pumping) pressure and diastolic (resting) pressure, respectively.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q10 - Cause of the first prominent heart sound

questiontext.text: During each cardiac cycle, which mechanical event is directly associated with the production of the first heart sound (lub)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The two prominent clinical heart sounds heard with a stethoscope are produced by the closure of specific heart valves.

Step 2: Evaluation of Acoustic Events
The first heart sound (lub) is caused by the simultaneous closure of the atrioventricular (tricuspid and bicuspid) valves at the onset of ventricular systole. In contrast, the second heart sound (dub) corresponds to the closure of the semilunar valves at the onset of ventricular diastole.

Final Answer: The first heart sound (lub) is associated with the closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves.

answer.text: Closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q11 - Definition and composition of human blood serum

questiontext.text: How is blood serum accurately defined in relation to human blood plasma?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plasma contains water, proteins (fibrinogen, globulins, albumins), dissolved nutrients, electrolytes, and factors required for blood coagulation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Serum Composition
When blood clots, fibrinogen and other clotting factors are consumed in forming the insoluble fibrin meshwork. The remaining clear straw-colored fluid that separates from the clot is plasma devoid of clotting factors, defined as serum.

Final Answer: Serum is defined as plasma without the clotting factors.

answer.text: Whole blood without formed elements and glucose
Fluid matrix containing only fibrinogen and platelets

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q12 - Secretory products and role of basophil granulocytes

questiontext.text: Which substances are secreted by basophils during inflammatory reactions in the human body?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Basophils are granulocytes with coarse granules that play critical roles in inflammatory and allergic reactions.

Step 2: Evaluation of Secretory Products
Basophils secrete chemical mediators including histamine (a vasodilator), serotonin (a vasoconstrictor), and heparin (an anticoagulant), all of which participate in mediating inflammatory reactions.

Final Answer: Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, and heparin during inflammatory reactions.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q13 - Primary immune function of eosinophil granulocytes

questiontext.text: What are the primary physiological roles associated with eosinophils in human peripheral blood?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Eosinophils are granulocytes with bilobed nuclei and prominent cytoplasmic granules that take up acidic stains, constituting 2 to 3 per cent of total white blood cells.

Step 2: Evaluation of Functional Roles
Eosinophils function primarily in resisting parasitic infections and are characteristically elevated during and associated with allergic reactions.

Final Answer: Eosinophils function to resist infections and are associated with allergic reactions.

answer.text: Resisting infections and participating in allergic reactions

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q14 - Major phagocytic cells among human white leucocytes

questiontext.text: Which types of leucocytes function actively as phagocytic cells to destroy foreign organisms entering the human body?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phagocytosis is an innate defense mechanism in which specialized white blood cells engulf and digest foreign microbes and cellular debris.

Step 2: Evaluation of Phagocytic Leucocytes
Among circulating leucocytes, neutrophils (granulocytes constituting 60 to 65 per cent) and monocytes (agranulocytes constituting 6 to 8 per cent) are phagocytic cells that engulf and destroy invading microorganisms.

Final Answer: Neutrophils and monocytes are the major phagocytic cells that destroy foreign organisms.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q15 - Sequential enzymatic steps in blood clot formation

questiontext.text: In the cascade mechanism of blood coagulation, which enzyme is directly responsible for converting inactive soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Blood coagulation involves an enzyme cascade where inactive precursors are sequentially converted into active enzymes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cascade Steps
The enzyme complex thrombokinase activates inactive prothrombin into thrombin. Thrombin then acts directly as the proteolytic enzyme that converts soluble fibrinogen in plasma into insoluble fibrin threads to form the clot coagulum.

Final Answer: Thrombin directly converts inactive fibrinogen into active fibrin threads.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q16 - Essential divalent mineral cation in blood coagulation

questiontext.text: Which mineral cation plays an essential and indispensable role at multiple stages in the cascade mechanism of blood clotting?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The blood clotting cascade requires specific mineral cofactors to facilitate enzymic conversions and complex assemblies.

Step 2: Evaluation of Ion Function
Calcium ions (\(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\)) are required as an essential cofactor for the activation of clotting factors, including the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin and subsequent polymerization of fibrin.

Final Answer: Calcium ions play a critical and indispensable role in blood clotting.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q17 - Medical prevention of erythroblastosis foetalis condition

questiontext.text: How can the development of erythroblastosis foetalis be prevented in an Rh-negative mother delivering an Rh-positive newborn?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During delivery of an Rh-positive infant, foetal erythrocytes can leak into maternal Rh-negative blood, stimulating the mother's immune system to produce anti-Rh antibodies that threaten subsequent Rh-positive pregnancies.

Step 2: Evaluation of Prophylaxis
This sensitization is prevented by administering exogenous anti-Rh antibodies (Rh-immunoglobulin) to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child, destroying any entered foetal Rh-positive RBCs before maternal immune memory is triggered.

Final Answer: Erythroblastosis foetalis is prevented by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child.

answer.text: Administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after delivery of the first child
Administering Rh antigens to the mother prior to her subsequent pregnancy
Transfusing Rh-positive whole blood to the mother during early gestation
Providing immunosuppressive drugs to the foetus during the final trimester

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q18 - ABO blood group compatibility for safe transfusion

questiontext.text: A recipient with blood group B requires an urgent blood transfusion. From which donor blood groups can this individual safely receive blood?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A recipient cannot receive donor red blood cells that possess surface antigens against which the recipient carries plasma antibodies.

Step 2: Evaluation of Compatibility
An individual with blood group B has antigen B on erythrocytes and anti-A antibodies in plasma. Blood from group B donors (having antigen B) and group O donors (having no ABO surface antigens) will not react with the recipient's anti-A antibodies and can be safely transfused.

Final Answer: A group B recipient can safely receive blood from group B and group O donors.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q19 - Structural composition and origin of interstitial tissue fluid

questiontext.text: How does the composition of interstitial fluid (tissue fluid) differ from that of circulating blood plasma?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
As blood flows through capillaries, hydrostatic pressure forces water and small solutes into intercellular spaces, while continuous capillary walls retain large molecules and cells.

Step 2: Evaluation of Interstitial Fluid Features
Interstitial fluid contains the same mineral distribution as plasma and facilitates nutrient and gas exchange, but it is largely devoid of larger plasma proteins and formed elements, which remain inside capillary vessels.

Final Answer: Interstitial fluid lacks larger plasma proteins and most formed elements while retaining a mineral distribution identical to plasma.

answer.text: It contains higher concentrations of fibrinogen and red blood cells than plasma
It lacks larger plasma proteins and most formed elements but has a similar mineral distribution
It is completely devoid of dissolved glucose, amino acids, and minerals
It contains higher albumin concentration and lower water content than plasma

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q20 - Specialized lymphatic vessels for intestinal lipid absorption

questiontext.text: Through which specialized lymphatic vessels are dietary fats absorbed in the human intestinal villi?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Dietary lipids are emulsified and digested into micelles in the small intestine, resynthesized into chylomicrons inside enterocytes, and absorbed into the lymphatic network.

Step 2: Evaluation of Lymphatic Structures
In the intestinal villi, specialized blind-ended central lymphatic capillaries known as lacteals absorb chylomicrons and transport fatty lymph into the lymphatic circulation.

Final Answer: Dietary fats are absorbed through lacteals present in the intestinal villi.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q21 - Vertebrate groups exhibiting incomplete double circulation pattern

questiontext.text: In which groups of vertebrates does the heart pump out mixed blood from a single ventricle, exhibiting incomplete double circulation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vertebrate hearts exhibit evolutionary adaptations: fishes have a 2-chambered heart (single circulation); amphibians and reptiles have 3 chambers (incomplete double circulation); birds and mammals have 4 chambers (complete double circulation).

Step 2: Evaluation of 3-Chambered Heart
Amphibians and reptiles (with the exception of crocodiles) possess a 3-chambered heart with two atria and a single ventricle. Oxygenated blood from respiratory organs and deoxygenated blood from the body enter separate atria but mix within the single ventricle before being pumped out.

Final Answer: Amphibians and reptiles (except crocodiles) exhibit incomplete double circulation with mixed ventricular blood.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q22 - Natural anatomical pacemaker of the human heart

questiontext.text: Why is the sino-atrial node (SAN) designated as the natural pacemaker of the human heart?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cardiac nodal tissue is autoexcitable, meaning it spontaneously generates action potentials without external neurogenic stimulation.

Step 2: Evaluation of SAN Properties
Although multiple regions of the nodal system can generate action potentials, the sino-atrial node (SAN) generates the highest frequency of action potentials (70 to 75 per minute). Consequently, it dictates the rhythm of atrial and ventricular contractions and sets the pace for the entire heart.

Final Answer: The sino-atrial node is called the pacemaker because it generates the maximum number of action potentials (70 to 75 per minute) to set the cardiac pace.

answer.text: It conducts impulses directly into the ventricular myocardium without delay
It generates the maximum number of action potentials (\(70\text{--}75\text{ min}^{-1}\)) to set the cardiac pace
It has the thickest muscular myocardium among all cardiac chambers
It contracts with greater mechanical force than ventricular muscle

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q23 - Percentage increment in ventricular filling during atrial systole

questiontext.text: During the resting human cardiac cycle, by approximately what percentage does atrial systole increase the flow of blood into the ventricles?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
During joint diastole, blood flows passively from the great veins through the open atrioventricular valves into the ventricles, filling the majority of ventricular capacity.

Step 2: Evaluation of Atrial Contraction
Simultaneous contraction of both atria (atrial systole) following an action potential from the sino-atrial node squeezes the remaining blood into the ventricles, increasing ventricular blood flow by approximately 30 per cent.

Final Answer: Atrial systole increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by about 30 per cent.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q24 - Electrical conduction pathway across the human myocardium

questiontext.text: What is the correct anatomical pathway for the conduction of cardiac action potentials through the human heart?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
An orderly sequence of electrical excitation is essential for synchronized contraction of atria followed by ventricles.

Step 2: Evaluation of Conduction Pathway
The impulse originates in the sino-atrial node (SAN) in the right atrium, travels to the atrio-ventricular node (AVN), continues through the atrio-ventricular bundle (AV bundle / bundle of His), divides into right and left bundle branches, and spreads throughout the ventricular myocardium via Purkinje fibres.

Final Answer: The conduction sequence is Sino-atrial node \(\rightarrow\) Atrio-ventricular node \(\rightarrow\) Atrio-ventricular bundle \(\rightarrow\) Purkinje fibres.

answer.text: Sino-atrial node \(\rightarrow\) Atrio-ventricular node \(\rightarrow\) Atrio-ventricular bundle \(\rightarrow\) Purkinje fibres
Atrio-ventricular node \(\rightarrow\) Sino-atrial node \(\rightarrow\) Purkinje fibres \(\rightarrow\) AV bundle
Sino-atrial node \(\rightarrow\) Purkinje fibres \(\rightarrow\) AV bundle \(\rightarrow\) Atrio-ventricular node
Atrio-ventricular bundle \(\rightarrow\) Sino-atrial node \(\rightarrow\) Atrio-ventricular node \(\rightarrow\) Purkinje fibres

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q25 - Calculation of human cardiac output from resting parameters

questiontext.text: If a healthy adult individual has a resting heart rate of 70 beats per minute and a stroke volume of \(70\text{ mL}\) per beat, what is the total cardiac output?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Resting heart rate (\(\text{HR}\)) is 70 beats per minute. Stroke volume (\(\text{SV}\)) pumped by each ventricle per contraction is \(70\text{ mL}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Cardiac output (\(\text{CO}\)) is defined as the volume of blood pumped out by each ventricle per minute, given by the formula: \[\text{CO} = \text{Stroke Volume} \times \text{Heart Rate}\]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values into the equation: \[\text{CO} = 70\text{ mL/beat} \times 70\text{ beats/min} = 4900\text{ mL min}^{-1}\]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The units are volume per unit time (\(\text{mL min}^{-1}\)), which is consistent with resting physiological cardiac output of approximately 5 litres per minute.

Final Answer: The cardiac output is \(4900\text{ mL min}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q26 - Electrical depolarization represented by standard ECG P wave

questiontext.text: In a standard electrocardiogram (ECG), what physiological event is represented by the P-wave?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
An electrocardiogram is a graphic recording of the electrical potentials generated by cardiac muscle during each cardiac cycle.

Step 2: Evaluation of Waveforms
The P-wave represents the electrical excitation (depolarisation) of the atria, which spreads from the sino-atrial node across the atrial musculature and leads directly to atrial contraction (atrial systole).

Final Answer: The P-wave represents the depolarisation of both atria.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q27 - Physiological event represented by the ECG QRS complex

questiontext.text: In a standard electrocardiogram, what does the QRS complex represent?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The QRS complex is the most prominent deflection in a standard electrocardiogram recording.

Step 2: Evaluation of Ventricular Activation
The QRS complex corresponds to the depolarisation of the ventricles as the action potential sweeps through the bundle of His and Purkinje fibres. Ventricular contraction begins shortly after the Q wave and marks the onset of ventricular systole.

Final Answer: The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q28 - Physiological significance of the ECG T wave

questiontext.text: In a standard electrocardiogram, what does the T-wave signify, and what event does its termination mark?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Following muscular excitation and contraction, cardiac myocytes must repolarise back to their resting membrane potential before another contraction can occur.

Step 2: Evaluation of Repolarisation Phase
The T-wave represents the repolarisation of the ventricles, reflecting the return of ventricular musculature from an excited state to a resting state. The conclusion of the T-wave clinically marks the end of ventricular systole.

Final Answer: The T-wave signifies ventricular repolarisation, and its end marks the end of systole.

answer.text: Depolarisation of the ventricles; beginning of ventricular systole
Repolarisation of the ventricles; end of ventricular systole
Repolarisation of the atria; end of atrial systole
Depolarisation of the atria; beginning of atrial systole

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_MCQ_Q29 - Histological difference in tunica media between blood vessels

questiontext.text: How does the tunica media of a vein structurally compare to that of an artery of similar caliber?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
